children: This summer's successive heatwaves could shave 0.1 percentage points off French economic growth on average this year, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
The ministry, however, stressed this was just a mere estimate at this stage and not an official update of its forecast for French growth, which currently stands at 0.7% for 2026.

Last week, the INSEE statistics agency revised growth for the second quarter of 2026 from 0.2% in an initial reading down to 0.0%, after the euro zone's second-biggest economy contracted by 0.2% in the first quarter.
Finance Minister Roland Lescure said last week that the INSEE downgrade "is the first impact of the horrible summer that we had."

The INSEE downgrade puts the government's full-year growth forecast of 0.7% all but out of reach as the economy would need to grow 0.5% in both the third and fourth quarters to reach it, according to INSEE.

Lescure told an economics conference last week that his ministry would need to factor in a likely weak third quarter when it updated France's growth and deficit forecasts in September before presenting the 2027 budget bill in early October.
